title: Never Split the Difference
author: Chris Voss with Tahl Raz
blurb: Chris Voss spent years as the FBI's lead international kidnapping negotiator. In this book he argues that most negotiation advice gets people wrong. We are not calm, rational deal makers. We are emotional creatures who decide with our feelings first. So the best negotiators don't argue harder. They listen better. Voss calls this tactical empathy: understanding the other side's feelings and showing them you understand. He turns it into practical tools you can use anywhere, from salary talks to buying a car to getting your kids to bed. These tools include repeating someone's last words back to them, naming their emotions out loud, inviting them to say no, and asking open questions that start with how or what. The goal is never a lazy compromise. It is uncovering hidden information that changes everything.
